## Zoning & Development Analysis: 6247 N Rockwell St (PIN 13012120090000)

---

### 1. Zoning District

This parcel is zoned **RS-2** (Residential Single-Unit, Detached House). [5] The RS-2 district is one of three RS districts differentiated primarily by minimum lot area requirements and floor area ratio — it is intended for areas characterized predominantly by detached houses on individual lots. [5]

**Verify:** Chicago's official Zoning Map at [gisapps.chicago.gov/ZoningMapWeb](https://gisapps.chicago.gov/ZoningMapWeb/?liab=1&config=zoning) — enter the address or PIN 13012120090000.

---

### 2. Can I Build a Two-Flat Here?

**Almost certainly no, under standard RS-2 rules — but there is one narrow exception to explore.**

RS-2 is a single-unit detached house district; its base purpose is one dwelling unit per lot. [5] However, [2] provides a specific exemption: in the **RS-3** district (not RS-2), the minimum lot area per unit may be reduced to 1,500 sq ft per unit — allowing a two-unit building — when 60% or more of zoning lots on the same block face are already improved with multi-unit buildings, *or* when the property falls within "Predominance of the Block" boundaries under [2].

That exemption is written for RS-3, not RS-2. Your parcel is RS-2, which carries a stricter minimum lot area per unit standard. Since the zone_definition data was not returned in this query, I cannot state the exact RS-2 minimum lot area per unit figure with certainty. What I can confirm:

- The parcel's **land area is 4,125 sq ft** per Cook County Assessor data.
- RS-2 requires a larger minimum lot area per unit than RS-3 (which already exceeds 4,125 sq ft for two units at most densities). [2]
- The "Predominance of the Block" exemption in [2] is explicitly limited to RS-3.

**Bottom line:** A two-flat is not a permitted use as-of-right in RS-2. You would likely need a **rezoning to RS-3 or RT3.5/RT4** to pursue two units lawfully.

**Verify:** Contact the Chicago Department of Planning & Development (DPD) zoning counter at 121 N LaSalle St, or call 312-744-5777.

---

### 3. Key Bulk & Density Standards

Because the full zone_definition detail was not returned for RS-2 specifically, I can confirm the following from the Municipal Code and assessor data, but **cannot state all numeric standards with certainty** without the RS-2 schedule:

| Standard | What the Code Says | Source |
|---|---|---|
| **Minimum Lot Area per Unit** | RS districts are subject to minimum lot-area-per-unit standards; other factors (parking, height, unit size, lot config) may further limit density beyond the floor standard | [2] |
| **Density limitation** | "These standards are not to be interpreted as a guarantee that allowed densities can be achieved on every lot" | [2] |
| **Off-street parking location** | Must be on the same zoning lot as the dwelling units served; prohibited in side setbacks and within 20 ft of front property line | [3] |
| **Coach house height** | Max 22 ft building height; rooftop features also capped at 22 ft above grade | [4] |
| **Accessory structure in rear setback** | Max 15 ft height (except coach houses) | [4] |

**What I could not determine:** The exact RS-2 FAR, maximum building height, front/rear/side setback dimensions, and minimum lot area per unit figure — these are in the RS-2 bulk table (§ 17-2-0303 and the associated district schedule) but that table was not retrieved in this query.

**Verify:** The full RS-2 standards are in the Chicago Zoning Ordinance, Chapter 17-2, Table 17-2-0303. Access the Zoning Ordinance at [Chicago Municipal Code online](https://codelibrary.amlegal.com/codes/chicago/latest/chicago_il/0-0-0-2610963) or ask DPD.

### 5. Parking Requirement & Transit Reduction

In RS districts, off-street parking required for residential uses **must be located on the same zoning lot** as the dwelling units served. [3] Off-street parking is prohibited in side setbacks and within **20 feet of the front property line**, but is permitted in a required side setback when accessed via a permitted driveway from the front property line. [3]

The parcel currently has a **1-car garage** per assessor records.

**Transit-related parking reduction:** Because this parcel is **not in a TOD area** and the nearest CTA rail is 1.74 miles away (well beyond the Connected Communities Ordinance's proximity thresholds), no automatic transit-based parking reduction or waiver is available. Any parking reduction would require a separate administrative or zoning process.

**Verify:** Parking quantity minimums for RS-2 are in the Chicago Zoning Ordinance § 17-10-0200 (off-street parking quantity schedule). The location rules are in [3].

### 6. Coach House / Accessory Dwelling Unit (ADU)

**No — not permitted on this parcel under current regulations.**

[4] explicitly states: *"A building permit for a new coach house unit may not be issued for any RS-designated zoning lot unless it complies with Section 17-7-0570."* [1] establishes the ADU-Allowed RS Areas — a set of designated neighborhoods where coach houses and conversion units are permitted in single-family zones. This parcel is **not in an ADU-Allowed RS Area** per the regulatory data.

Key coach house standards that *would* apply if the parcel were in an ADU area — for reference:
- Max building height: **22 feet** [4]
- Rooftop features: max **22 feet** above grade [4]
